obligation: Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards (CFATS), including RBPS 8 Cyber
applies: No (authority lapsed; used as a voluntary benchmark)
basis: The plant holds about 35,000 lb of hydrogen peroxide in 50% solution, an Appendix A chemical of interest for theft and diversion (minimum concentration 35%, STQ 400 lb). The company filed a Top-Screen in 2008, was tiered, and operated under an approved Site Security Plan. The statutory authority expired on 2023-07-28 and 6 U.S.C. 621-629 is shown as omitted; CISA states it cannot enforce CFATS. RBPS 8 is used as a voluntary benchmark, and legacy CVI is still protected as a precaution

obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System rule
basis: Applies only to facilities required to have a security plan under 33 CFR Part 105 (101.605(a)). The plant is inland, with a rail siding and a truck rack and no marine transfer or dock

No final rule has been published. As proposed, the company (162 employees, under the SBA standard of 650 for NAICS 325998) would fall under the size criterion, and the CFATS-facility sector criterion is moot while CFATS is lapsed

The aqueous ammonia process holds 23,925 lb of ammonia (11,000 gal x 7.50 lb/gal x 29%) against the 20,000 lb threshold for ammonia (conc 20% or greater) in 68.130, so the process is covered (68.10(a); 68.115). Program 1 is not available because the worst-case release reaches public receptors (68.10(j)(2)); Program 3 does not apply because NAICS 325998 is not in 68.10(l)(1) and the process is not covered by OSHA PSM. Non-responding stationary source (68.90(b))
Not a final rule; the current Part 68 text governs. Tracked for planning

A release at or above a reportable quantity must be reported immediately, regardless of cause. The plant stores ammonia (RQ 100 lb, also an EPCRA extremely hazardous substance), sodium hypochlorite, sulfuric acid and hydrochloric acid in quantities far above their RQs

No chemical is at a listed concentration and threshold: 29% aqueous ammonia is below the 44% listing; 50% hydrogen peroxide is below the 52% listing; hydrochloric acid is listed only as anhydrous and sulfuric acid only as oleum; isopropyl alcohol stays at 7,205 lb (4 totes), under the 10,000 lb flammable liquid threshold. Coverage would follow if peroxide at 52% or higher were bought or the 4-tote cap were exceeded
